newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler sees Q4 incentives flat with Q3.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sees Q4 incentives flat with Q3.

text.p: Chrysler Corp Chief Financial Officer Gary Valade said Monday he expects the automaker's U.S. retail incentives to remain in the $675-$680 per vehicle range, roughly the same as the automaker's third quarter level.

Valade told reporters on a conference call following release of Chysler's third quarter earnings that lease incentives on the Jeep Grand Cherokee sport/utility vehicle have pushed up incentive spending in recent months.
"It has been successful, but it has cost us a few hundred dollars (per vehicle) of incentives," Valade said of the Jeep program.
Valade said despite the incentives, increasing competition has not produced a significant deterioration in Chrysler's Grand Cherokee profit margins.

He also said he anticipates that Chrysler will maintain its current share of the U.S. and Canadian vehicle market -- about 16.2 percent -- through the end of the year, but remains cautious about adding new capacity needed to increase its share significantly.
The company is adding 190,000 units worth of new truck capacity next year, including a new Dodge sport/utility vehicle, he said.
